cards.title: What is an API?
cards.content: An API (Application Programming Interface) allows different software systems to communicate with each other. In Python development, we often use APIs to fetch data from web services, interact with databases, or integrate third-party services like payment gateways.

content.question: Which HTTP method is typically used to retrieve data from an API?

cards.title: Using the Requests Library
cards.content:
The requests library is the standard way to make HTTP requests in Python.

import requests

response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/data')
print(response.json())

cards.title: Checking Status Codes
cards.content: To check if an HTTP request was successful in Python, we often verify that the response status code is equal to ___.

cards.title: Working with JSON Data
cards.content:
APIs commonly return data in JSON format. Python automatically parses JSON responses into native dictionaries using the .json() method.

data = response.json()
user_name = data.get('name')

cards.title: API Authentication
cards.content:
Many APIs require authentication to ensure secure access. This is typically done using API keys, Bearer tokens, or OAuth passed via request headers.

headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_TOKEN'}
response = requests.get('https://api.example.com/secure', headers=headers)
